clue.text: Adjutant's no end of a hermit in Africa

definitions.note: the adjutant is a large stork; the 's stands for 'is', linking it to the wordplay

indicators.note: no end of means the final letter of the hermit's title is cut off

parts.note: a marabout is a Muslim holy man or hermit in North Africa

explanation.surface: Someone's military aide is described as an endless desert holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adjutant' looks military but is the adjutant stork. MARABOUT loses its last letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjutant bird and the marabou are both names for the same big African stork.

clue.text: One is some form of understatement

definitions.text: One is some form of understatement

parts.words: One is some form of understatement
parts.note: the clue simply states that it is a figure of speech of deliberate understatement, as in litotes

explanation.definitionFit: In rhetoric this term names understatement, such as calling a disaster a bit of bother.

clue.text: Version I'd interchange on completion

annotationWithheld.why: Version I'd interchange on completion (9): no parse found that builds the answer from I'd, interchange and completion

clue.text: Potter's smooth little pig

explanation.surface: A pottery maker's glazed piglet.
explanation.walkthrough: Potter is Beatrix Potter, whose Tale of Pigling Bland features a small pig of that name; 'Potter's' frames the little pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild and unexciting means without sharp edges, and Pigling Bland is a piglet in a children's book.

clue.text: Shown to have no policy?

explanation.surface: Someone is revealed to lack insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something revealed is laid bare, and someone without insurance cover is unprotected.

clue.text: Like Ilium's towers, 4 from the waist up

explanation.surface: Troy's famous towers are compared with a body bared above the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: Marlowe's Faustus speaks of 'the topless towers of Ilium' (Troy), meaning too tall to see their tops. 4 refers to the answer at 4 down, UNCOVERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlowe called Troy's towers impossibly high, and a person bare above the waist has the same adjective.

clue.text: Army on march to river

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
Mar is the abbreviation for the month of March

explanation.surface: Soldiers set out on a march towards a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface treats march as marching; it is the month.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall in south-west England.

clue.text: Tropic zoo adapted for such primitive creatures

indicators.note: adapted means the letters of the two words are refashioned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tropical zoo is modified to house simple organisms.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes single-celled organisms such as amoebas.

clue.text: Work of Rousseau or Zola?

explanation.surface: Is this book by Rousseau or by Zola?
explanation.walkthrough: Rousseau wrote a treatise on education of this title; Zola's first name was Émile.
explanation.definitionFit: Rousseau's novel on education bears this title, and it is also the French novelist Zola's forename.

clue.text: Ghost of the tax-man, we hear, drops in

indicators.note: drops means the following short word is removed from the front
we hear tells us to take the official's title as spoken, respelt the way it sounds

parts.note: a tax inspector is a tax-man

explanation.surface: The ghost of a revenue official, rumour says, pays a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: INSPECTOR said aloud could be spelt INSPECTRE; 'drops' removes the IN at its front.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a phantom or apparition.

clue.text: In Hebridean island was one Greek settlement

indicators.note: In tells us one piece sits within the island's name

parts.note: Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Scottish island is claimed as a former Greek colony.
explanation.walkthrough: IONA is a small Scottish island famous for its abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionia was the coastal region of Asia Minor colonised by Greeks.

clue.text: Plant of this order from Corinth and 9?

explanation.surface: A plant grows in a classical style mixing Corinth and Ionia.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is IONIA: the Composite architectural order blends Ionic and Corinthian capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisies belong to the Compositae family, and the fifth classical column style combines Ionic and Corinthian features.

clue.text: One not suited for submarine work

definitions.text: One not suited for submarine work

parts.words: One not suited for submarine work
parts.note: unsuited reads as unfit, but means without a diving suit: someone exploring underwater in bare skin

explanation.definitionFit: A diver who swims without a diving suit or breathing gear works underwater wearing no suit.

clue.text: Finished the last of it in public

parts.note: something finished is over

indicators.note: the last of picks the final letter of the word it

explanation.surface: Someone drained the final drop where everyone could see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done openly is plain and unconcealed rather than secret.

clue.text: Highly-rated author?

parts.note: a celebrated writer, or the writer named after a bird that flies very high and fast

explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels, and the bird of that name flies at great height.

clue.text: Fast Indian trick mounted by acrobat

parts.note: fast and tight both mean firmly fixed
the Indian rope trick is a famous illusion of a boy climbing a rope rising into the air

explanation.surface: A quick Indian illusion performed by a gymnast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed, but it means fixed firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: A high wire stretched taut is climbed onto by circus performers.

clue.text: To give birth will thus provide copy

explanation.surface: Having a baby is described as making a duplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeding offspring and making a facsimile are both covered by this verb.

clue.text: One in back seat sees prang developing

indicators.note: developing means the letters of the fodder take a new form

explanation.surface: Someone riding in the back watches a car crash unfold.
explanation.walkthrough: A prang is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider who is not driving sits as a traveller, often behind the driver.

clue.text: Makes one sort of trust heretic is not a Trinity man

parts.note: a unit trust is one type of investment trust
an Arian followed Arius, condemned as a heretic for denying Christ's full divinity

explanation.surface: A dissenting believer who rejects the Trinity is a college outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: A unit trust is a British pooled investment fund. 'Trinity man' suggests a Cambridge college member.
explanation.definitionFit: Unitarians believe God is one person and reject the doctrine of three persons in one God.

clue.text: Descartes and Degas disguised as deserters

parts.note: the philosopher Descartes's first name was René

indicators.note: disguised means the painter's name has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Two French masters, a philosopher and a painter, go undercover as army runaways.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter's name is shuffled by 'disguised' and follows the philosopher's first name; the two famous Frenchmen are a surface decoy for army runaways.
explanation.definitionFit: Renegades are turncoats who abandon their side or cause.

clue.text: Teeth chatter in frenzy

indicators.note: in frenzy means the letters of the word chatter are thrown wildly about

explanation.surface: Someone's teeth rattle in a fit of panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed bar or wheel engaged by a catch.

clue.text: Rise of about one pound to doctor

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
one is the Roman numeral I
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A price goes up by about a pound when paid to the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb is an ascent, an upward movement.

clue.text: Hardy's flourishing partner?

parts.note: Oliver Hardy's comic partner was Stan Laurel, and laurel is a shrub that flourishes, as in the psalm's green one

explanation.definitionFit: The laurel plant is another name for this evergreen, recalling Laurel and Hardy.

clue.text: Habitat of llamas? Only if 5 ac

definitions.text: Habitat of llamas? Only if 5 ac

parts.words: Habitat of llamas? Only if 5 ac
parts.note: the woolly animals live in the Andes; only if 5 across is applied, cutting off the head letter, do they become Buddhist monks of a Himalayan land

explanation.definitionFit: Lamas are Buddhist monks in that Himalayan country; llama with its head letter cut becomes lama.

clue.text: Hence Arthur was in no hurry to reply

definitions.text: Hence Arthur was in no hurry to reply

parts.words: Hence Arthur was in no hurry to reply
parts.note: to interrupt rudely is to push in; Arthur took a slow boat to Avalon, so did not push in

explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur was borne to Avalon on a slow vessel, and to push rudely into a conversation uses the same word.

clue.text: But no such punishment for such excellent conduct

definitions.text: But no such punishment for such excellent conduct

parts.words: But no such punishment for such excellent conduct
parts.note: a severe sentence meant as a deterrent has this adjective, but so does faultless behaviour, which earns no penalty

explanation.definitionFit: Exemplary punishment warns others, while exemplary conduct is a model worth copying.

clue.text: Essayist's other name for prophet

explanation.surface: A writer of essays has an alias that also names a prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia, so 'Essayist's' gives Elia's; Elias is the Greek form of Elijah.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb's pen name was Elia, and the Old Testament prophet Elijah is called Elias in the New Testament.

clue.text: Introduction of Elgar's overture in concert

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed within the concert

parts.note: a Prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

indicators.note: overture means the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: An Elgar overture is played as the opening of a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are London's summer concert season, famous for Elgar's music.
explanation.definitionFit: A proem is a preface or opening passage of a book or speech.

clue.text: Painful farm work

explanation.surface: Agricultural labour is described as distressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A distressing experience is agonising, and breaking clods with a toothed frame is a field task.

clue.text: Zero rise, sadly, for the basket-maker

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O

indicators.note: sadly means the word rise is jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A craftsman weaving baskets gets no pay increase, which is unfortunate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' signals the anagram of the second word; 'basket-maker' reads as a weaver but is the willow the baskets are made from.
explanation.definitionFit: Willow shoots of this kind are the material woven into baskets.

clue.text: Plural pronouns in ancient Greek

parts.note: these is a plural demonstrative pronoun
us is a plural personal pronoun

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on plural pronouns in classical Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian hero who killed the Minotaur was a legendary figure of Greece.

clue.text: Such language for a tale of chivalry?

explanation.surface: A question about what to call the idiom of knightly stories.
explanation.definitionFit: French, Italian and Spanish are Latin-derived tongues of this family, and a medieval story of knightly adventure has the same name.
